at the time of the sacrifice. At the time the sacrifice is offered.
to the men of the ancestral house who offer on that day. The priests appointed over the Temple service on that day (Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 4:11).
the holy things of the Temple. The priestly gifts given in the Temple (see Hilchot Bikkurim 1:10).
a meal-offering against a meal-offering. One priest receives a whole meal-offering and in return the other receives another meal-offering, and they do not divide the meal-offerings themselves.
and likewise a woman and an androgynos. Who may eat lesser sacrifices (above halakhot 4-6, 9).
but a blemished priest... divides and eats. See also Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 6:12.
whether permanent or transient. For the details of the types of blemishes, see Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash chapter 8.
and the High Priest eats not by division but takes whatever he wishes. And takes his portion first (Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 5:12).

a tevul yom. An impure person who immersed; as long as the sun has not set on him he is in a mild state of impurity and forbidden to eat terumah and sacred offerings (Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTumot 10:1-2).

and one lacking atonement. A zav, a zavah, a woman after childbirth and a leper who have become pure of their impurity, and are forbidden to eat sacred offerings until they bring a sacrifice to complete their purification process (Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:1).

and an onen on the day of burial. One whose relative died is forbidden to serve and to eat sacred offerings on the day of burial, and at night afterward it is permitted (provided the burial was not on the day of death, Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 2:9-10).
who serves but does not eat, as we have explained. Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 2:8.
except a blemished priest, for it is specified in the Torah. See above halakhah 17.
whoever has no share in the meat has no share in the skins. The skins of most holy offerings that the priests acquire (above 5:19).

even if he was impure at the time of the sprinkling of blood and pure at the time of the burning of the fats. For example, the fats were burned at night after his sun had set, or one lacking atonement brought his sacrifice between the sprinkling and the burning.

the matter is in doubt whether he divides or does not divide. The doubt is whether it suffices that he be pure at the time of the services, or he must be pure from the beginning of the services to their end.

therefore if he seized, it is not taken from his hand. Because of the doubt he cannot claim a share in the sacrifice, and they do not give him a share. But if he took himself, what he took cannot be taken from him since perhaps it is due to him (for this principle see also Hilchot Bechorot 2:6, Hilchot Nizkei Mamon 9:11 and elsewhere).

a communal sacrifice that comes in impurity, even though the impure offer it. When most of the congregation (or the service vessels or the priests) are impure, the impure are permitted to offer sacrifices whose time is fixed (Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 4:9-10; this speaks of a case where the meat did not become impure, see Radbaz and Arukh HaShulchan 82:19).
from oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in the interpretation of the verses.
for this is a warning against eating the flesh of the burnt-offering. A warning not to eat. And from this verse they also learned the warning about misuse of sacred things (Hilchot Me'ilah 1:3).
its libations. The meal-offering of libations that comes with the burnt-offering (above 2:1-2).
all five join to make an olive's bulk. For liability to lashes if he ate them (and likewise for misuse if he benefited from them, Commentary on the Mishnah, Me'ilah 4:2).
the sacrificial fats. See above 1:18.
entirely to the altar. All of them are burned on the altar.
in the priests' meal-offering. The meal-offerings brought by priests are burned on the altar, and are not eaten like other meal-offerings (below 12:9).
from the flesh of the sin-offerings that are burned. Above 1:16.

before the sprinkling of the blood he is flogged. Even after the sprinkling of the blood one may not eat of the meat until the sacrificial fats are burned (above 9:11, but one is not flogged for this, Mishneh LaMelekh).
whether lesser or more stringent. Lesser sacrifices and most holy offerings.
and the bread. That comes with the thanksgiving-offering (above 9:17-18).
outside the Temple court. Above 10:3.
outside Jerusalem. Above 10:5.
and the same is true of the flesh of a sin-offering and guilt-offering or the remainders of meal-offerings. Their prohibition is equal.
outside its partition. Outside the boundary of the place where it is permitted to eat it.
as we have explained in Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot. 5:9.
